Canadian retail sales rose 3.5% to $864.0B in the 12 months to July 2026, with Ontario, Quebec and Alberta leading
## Executive summary
- Total retail sales in Canada (Retail trade [44-45], unadjusted) were $864.0B in the 12 months to July 2026, up from $834.7B in the 12 months before: a change of +$29.3B, or +3.5%, in the published totals.
- The provinces add up to Canada, and the store types add up to retail trade; the part of the change no published part holds is $0.0B.
- Ontario (+$10.2B), Quebec (+$6.2B) and Alberta (+$5.9B) account for most of the change by province; general merchandise retailers (+$8.1B), health and personal care retailers (+$6.6B) and gasoline stations (+$6.1B) lead by store type.
- Only the Northwest Territories fell among the provinces (-$47.0M, -4.6%), and furniture, home furnishings, electronics and appliance retailers fell by $1.7B (-3.9%).
- The engine's grade is a process grade: it measures month-to-month noise in 36 monthly totals and is not a test of the published total.
## The headline: a published total up 3.5%, described rather than tested
The 12-month total of Total retail sales rose from $834.7B to $864.0B, a change of +$29.3B (+3.5%). Statistics Canada publishes the figure, so the engine describes it instead of testing it; the grade beside it, NOT ENOUGH DATA, grades the month-to-month noise of the 24 monthly totals behind the average month, and says nothing about whether the published change is real.
## What drove it: Ontario, Quebec and Alberta, and three store types
By province, Ontario added $10.2B (+3.2% on its own year), Quebec $6.2B (+3.4%) and Alberta $5.9B (+5.6%). Alberta grew fastest of the three. By store type, general merchandise retailers added $8.1B (+6.7%), health and personal care retailers $6.6B (+9.5%) and gasoline stations $6.1B (+8.1%). A contribution says where the change sits, not what caused it.

## Other findings: the parts that fell
The Northwest Territories moved against the national change, down $47.0M (-4.6%). Among store types, furniture, home furnishings, electronics and appliance retailers fell $1.7B (-3.9%) and building material and garden equipment dealers fell $144.7M (-0.3%).

## Scenarios
The engine's forecast for August 2026 is $73.0B, with an 80% range of $72.4B to $77.7B. The forecast repeats the same month from last year, which is the benchmark the engine compares every model with; it was back-tested at four horizons, held 21 of 23 at 1 month, 19 of 21 at 3 months, 17 of 18 at 6 months and 11 of 12 at 12 months. Use it as a guide, not a plan.
## What to do
1. Read the contributions by store type before the national figure: three types carry $20.8B of the $29.3B.
2. Check the Northwest Territories and the furniture and appliance segment against their own sales reports; they are the two places that fell.
3. Re-run the report when the next month is published; the 12-month windows move by one month.
## Risks and what the data cannot say
- The data cannot say why sales rose; the contributions describe where the change sits.
- Sales are in current dollars, so some of the +3.5% is price, which this file does not separate.
- Suppressed cells (5,430 in the file) are left out of the parts; the engine reports what no published part holds, $0.0B here.
